Front: JVM memory: heap vs stack, and what causes StackOverflowError vs OutOfMemoryError: Java heap space?
Back: The heap is shared by all threads and holds objects and arrays; the garbage collector reclaims unreachable ones (sized with -Xms/-Xmx). Each thread has its own stack of method frames (locals, references, return addresses). StackOverflowError: the thread stack is exhausted, usually by deep or infinite recursion. OutOfMemoryError: Java heap space: a new allocation can't fit in the heap. Class metadata lives in Metaspace, outside the heap.

Front: What are the class-loading phases, and when does a static block run?
Back: Loading (a class loader finds the bytecode: bootstrap → platform → application/classpath), then Linking: verification, preparation (static fields get default values) and resolution, then Initialization, which runs static initializers and static blocks once, on first active use. For the class that holds main(), static init runs before main(). A class present at compile time but missing at runtime gives NoClassDefFoundError; Class.forName("x") gives ClassNotFoundException. The JIT later compiles hot methods to native code.

Front: What does SpringApplication.run() do, and how do you see why something was or wasn't auto-configured?
Back: It prepares the Environment, creates the ApplicationContext, registers bean definitions (component scan + @Configuration/@Bean), applies conditional autoconfiguration, creates the beans and injects dependencies, starts the embedded server (Tomcat for web apps), runs CommandLineRunner/ApplicationRunner callbacks, then the app is ready. @SpringBootApplication = @SpringBootConfiguration + @EnableAutoConfiguration + @ComponentScan. Start with --debug to print the CONDITIONS EVALUATION REPORT (positive/negative matches). spring-boot-starter-actuator adds operational endpoints like GET /actuator/health → {"status":"UP"}.
